answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents lock collateral in a secure vault before transacting. Randomly sampled multi-agent auditor committees cross-examine state logs signed by each agent's digital quill. If topological cut verifications reveal clustered, coordinated collusion, the protocol executes automated stake slashing, forfeiting deposits and redirecting protocol nectar to honest auditors. Because audit cut verification scales across network subgraphs, attacking requires a superlinear attacker cost relative to the number of deployed identities.
